chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addab from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asbahani from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Abi Harun al-Abdi from Abi Sa'id al-Khudri who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting on a certain day, and with him were some of his companions, among them Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him). He said: 'Whoever says
"La ilaha illallah" (There is no god but Allah)
Two men from his companions said: "We say "La ilaha illallah"."

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) replied: "The testimony of "There is no god but Allah" is accepted only from this one (Ali) and his Shia (followers) who have taken the covenant of our Lord."
The two men said: "We say "La ilaha illallah"."

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) placed his hand on the head of Ali (peace be upon him) and said: "The sign of that is that you should not break your oath to him, nor sit in his place, nor reject his words."
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ali ibn Abi Talib in accepting the testimony of 'La ilaha illallah' according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Wilayah* (spiritual authority) as the essential condition for the validity of the Shahada. The Prophet’s gesture of placing his hand on Ali’s head serves as a physical sign (*Ayah*) of his designation, while the criteria for acceptance—loyalty, non-usurpation, and belief in his teachings—underscore the inseparable link between monotheism and allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. al-Hassan Mu’addab from Ahmad b. Ali al-Asbahani from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b.

Ishaq from Abi Harun al-’Abdi from Abi Sa’eed al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of Allah (sw) was sitting on a certain day, and with him were some of his companions, among them Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS).
So he (sw) said, "Whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' (there is no god but Allah) shall enter Paradise."
Two men from his companions said, "We say 'La ilaha illallah'".
The Messenger of Allah (sw) replied, "The testimony of 'There is no god but Allah' is accepted only from this person and his Shia (followers) who have taken the covenant of our Lord."
The two men said, "We say 'La ilaha illallah'".

Then the Messenger of Allah (sw) placed his hand on the head of Ali (AS) and said, "The sign (of acceptance of the statement of La ilaha illallah) is that one should not break oaths given to him, nor sit in his place or reject his words."
